text.p: French courier operator, Chronopost, said it would be opening dedicated facilities at Marseille airport towards end-1997.
"The project we have in mind will give us direct airside access for a swift and efficient throughput of traffic," a Chronopost official told Reuters.
At present, Chronopost occupies facilities at Vitrolles, situated a few miles from the airport, the official added.
"We have no precise details at this stage on what the facilities will comprise, the surface area they will cover nor investment costs," he added.
Chronopost is 66 percent-owned by the French post office and 34 percent by French aviation group, TAT SA.

The sole carrier of Chronopost freight in and out of Marseille is L'Aeropostale -- also owned by the French post offcie -- which operates Boeing 737-300QC (quick change) freighter services from Paris-CDG to the southern France gateway.

L'Aeropostale generated 9,544 tonnes of airfreight at Marseille airport last year, up 26 percent on 1995 levels, airport authority figures showed. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+ 7706
